messages:
Ashley: Hey — I have request_id=abc123 and trace_id=7f4b9e. Console is collapsing the request_id column for that timeframe. What's the fastest path to the raw log lines?
Matt: If the console view is being unhelpful, try the Advanced Logs query: `request_id:abc123` or `trace.id:7f4b9e`. But note some edge logs don't index request_id.
Sana: FWIW when it's an edge -> pod hop I usually stern the proxy/pod and grep:
```
stern -n prod 'proxy|envoy' --since 15m | rg abc123
```
Matt: Another quick flow: from the trace UI copy the span link (Share -> Copy span link) -> the span link encodes span_id. Then search logs for `span_id:SPANID`. Console sometimes links them automatically.
Ashley: Good call. If span -> log link is missing, do we have a fallback service mapping?
Sana: Yeah check the edge access log enrichment. If `X-Request-Id` isn't forwarded into app logs, you'll miss direct matches. In that case: 1) find the span/trace, 2) pick a timestamp window, 3) stern the related pods and grep time-range.
observability-bot: Quick pointer — dashboard: https://console.redwood.com/dashboards/ops/request-journey (links traces -> logs when span->log link exists).
Matt: If console search is flaky you can hit internal log API: `curl -G "https://logs.internal/api/v1/search" --data-urlencode "q=request_id:abc123"` — useful for automation.
Ashley: Any kubectl one-liners if I know the app label but not the pod name?
Sana: Yup: run
```
kubectl get pods -l app=my-service -n prod -o name | xargs -n1 -I{} kubectl logs {} -c app --tail=200 | rg abc123
```
Matt: Pro tip — if tracing sampling dropped the trace, search by request header / proxy access logs (they're more likely to have the request id). Also check `edge-proxy` logs since they live before sampling.
Ashley: Thanks, I'll try stern first and then the API fallback. @Sana please file a tiny PR to add request_id in access log enrichment for the edge if it's missing.
Sana: Ack — will open PR + add unit test for log enrichment config. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: FYI scheduled retention job will rotate logs older than 30d, so act fast if older than that.
Ashley: Got it — saved my bacon. If I get stuck I'll paste the span link here.
Matt: If you paste the span link I can extract span/trace ids and run a quick cluster grep for you.
Sana: Also adding a small checklist to the observability runbook: trace->span link -> span_id -> console search -> stern fallback -> raw kubectl logs.
Ashley: Perfect — thanks everyone!
